Cliff Richard Sees Streaming Surge Following GTA 6 Trailer Appearance

An Unexpected Musical Revival

British singer Cliff Richard is experiencing a significant surge in popularity at age 86, following the inclusion of his 1976 hit 'Devil Woman' in the latest promotional material for Rockstar Games' upcoming title, Grand Theft Auto 6. Since the release of the extended look at the game, daily streams of the track have increased by 325%.

A Disconnected Success

Despite the massive exposure provided by one of the gaming industry's most anticipated releases, Richard has admitted he was largely unaware of the context surrounding his song's resurgence. In an interview with The Times, the veteran musician expressed confusion regarding the nature of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, initially characterizing it as a game show. He noted that he was alerted to the trend by family members who recognized his voice in the promotional footage.

Impact on Legacy

Richard acknowledged that while he belongs to an earlier era of music, the attention brought by contemporary platforms helps bridge the gap between his long-standing career and modern audiences. The singer expressed appreciation for the continued relevance of his work in today's media landscape.

Context for Players

Rockstar Games has confirmed that the soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature a blend of classic hits and contemporary artists, including appearances by musicians like Yung Lean and Travis Scott. This curation strategy is designed to build the atmosphere for the game's depiction of Vice City.

Further Information

Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently scheduled for a global release on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles. Readers interested in the official soundtrack announcements and promotional updates can visit the official Rockstar Games website at https://www.ign.com/articles/devil-woman-singer-cliff-richard-didnt-know-gta-6.
